summary: We developed LifeLine, a website where astronauts track, and monitor their mental and physical health while in space. In addition of the website, we developed interactive games built inside the website to make health tracking more fun and convenient to astronauts. We built a mini reaction time game to test astronauts hand-eye coordination, and floating body with multiple pulse points. The reaction game addresses the challenge of testing neurological health/cognitive functions in astronauts by providing a fun game. The faster they can click/react to the buttons, the better score they will receive prompting them to continue playing, thus enhancing their cognition. Contrasly, the free body diagram allows the inputs of the user, and the healthy adult at a similar height and age to judge how healthy they are compared to the norm. In a mental health aspect, we pondered that conversation and seeking therapies are extremely vital for astronauts. But with the constant stress on their minds, we wanted another way for them to express themselves in a safe and private matter. So we created a logging journal that they must write everyday, talking about how they are feeling at the moment. Ultimately, we believe that this project is extremely relevant because of the advancement of astrological exploration. The health of astronauts becomes increasingly more important. So LifeLine will allow astronauts to continue exploring while being safe.
details:
Project Lifeline was built from the prompt of health monitoring software for astronauts in space. We wanted to solve the problem of the difficulty to track and maintain your health as an astronaut in space while worrying about space and rocket complications, that health feels like a lower priority at the time. We created software that makes it easier and more convenient for astronauts to take care of their health, monitor it, and ensure that they have no outstanding medical conditions. We created a free and open-source website that utilizes the preexisting machines on the ISS (the International Space Station), such as:

  • A blood pressure pump
  • A DEXA scan machine, measures bone density
  • MOFSET radiation dosimeter, measuring radiation in astronauts

We planned to connect each and every machine to the website to interconnect them in software that astronauts can conveniently view from any location and at any time. We utilized HTML and JavaScript for the main apparatus, and we specialized in JavaScript for the reaction time tester game. By using the criteria and the objectives of the project prompt that was given to us by NASA Space Apps, we decided to gamify the whole health monitoring system by creating little mini games inside, such as the reaction time tester, which tests hand-eye coordination and speed while being a fun game.

Also, other aspects include the free-body diagram, with areas where you can press and see different areas of your body and see which areas need the most support, with accurate information given by the machines and the inputs you, the user, put in.

Some factors that our team considered were space radiation, isolation, confinement, or distance from Earth, and mental health overall for astronauts. We felt like physical health and mental health were holistically the same in the sense that if you have bad mental health, you're not going to perform well, just the same as with physical health.
